extracted.intended_audience: researchers/authors preparing and submitting articles to arXiv
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and requirements for preparing and uploading articles (preprints) to the arXiv repository, including allowed file formats, figure handling, metadata, timing, and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitter must be a registered author
rubrics_metrics.description: We accept submissions only from registered authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only accounts of registered authors may submit. Authors should ensure they have registered before attempting to submit.

rubrics_metrics.name: License requirement for distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitters must grant arXiv.org a non-exclusive and irrevocable license to distribute or certify that the work is available under another license that conveys these rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must either grant arXiv the stated license or confirm the article is under a license that gives arXiv equivalent distribution rights; this is required at submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowed text formats (preferred order)
rubrics_metrics.description: Your submission to the archive must be in one of the following formats (listed in order of preference): (La)TeX, AMS(La)TeX, PDFLaTeX; PDF; PostScript; HTML with JPEG/PNG/GIF images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: arXiv's goal is to store highly portable stable formats; TeX/LaTeX is preferred because it does not hide information. Choose the best-supported format for long-term archival quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit certain TeX-derived outputs (prohibited formats)
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that for this and other reasons we will not accept dvi, PS, or PDF created from TeX/LaTeX source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you work in TeX/LaTeX, submit the source (or follow PDFLaTeX workflow) rather than uploading dvi/PS or PDFs generated from TeX in unsupported ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word-processor submissions guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Users of word processors such as Microsoft Word (versions prior to Word 2007) should save their documents as PDF and submit that.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If using Word or another word processor, produce a clean PDF for submission. Do not submit scanned documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scanned documents not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Note also that we will not accept scanned documents, regardless of format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if you produce a PDF by scanning, it will be rejected. Provide digital source or properly generated PDF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure file formats allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Figures for a submission can be in a number of common formats: PostScript (PS/EPS), JPEG, GIF or PNG, PDF figures (only with PDFLaTeX).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PS/EPS for line drawings/plots, JPEG for photos, GIF/PNG for non-photographic images/bitmaps. PDF figures only when using PDFLaTeX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figure size and download considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: If figure files are too large, then readers with poor network connections will not be able to download them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce figure file sizes where possible to accommodate users with poor connections (information on submission sizes and bitmapping help is available). If you have problems with a large submission, contact arXiv administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not omit figures/tables/sections or submit abstract-only
rubrics_metrics.description: Please note that we do not accept submissions with omitted figures, tables or sections. We also do not accept 'abstract only' submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All substantive content referenced (figures, tables, sections) must be included; linking to external servers for omitted content is not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: If including figures with LaTeX source, use standard packages
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submit figures with your (La)TeX source, use standard macro packages (e.g., the graphics and graphicx packages) so that the figures will appear in the document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use widely-used packages to ensure arXiv processing can render your figures. arXiv administration cannot provide TeX help—seek colleagues' assistance if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name character restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: arXiv will accept only the following characters in file names: a-z A-Z 0-9 _ + - . , =. The presence of any other character (e.g. spaces, question marks, asterisks, etc.) will cause the system to reject the file upload or submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure filenames contain only the allowed characters to avoid automated rejection. These restrictions ensure portability and minimize archival risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: File name and extension case sensitivity
rubrics_metrics.description: File names and extensions are also case sensitive on our system. The file names Figure1.PDF and figure1.pdf are not the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure internal file references (e.g., LaTeX figure inclusion commands) match case exactly to avoid broken links on arXiv, regardless of your local OS case-sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of data sets and ancillary files is limited
rubrics_metrics.description: There are limited facilities for including data sets and ancillary files (data, programs, etc.) which are associated with articles submitted to arXiv.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See separate instructions about including data sets and ancillary files; do not assume full support for arbitrary supplemental materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title/abstract metadata preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: See separate instructions on the preparation of separate title/abstract information. This information is used on the abstract pages, in announcements, in RSS feeds, and to support searching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare concise, accurate title and abstract metadata since it is public-facing and used for discovery and announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check submissions and read system messages before finalizing
rubrics_metrics.description: Before you make the final 'Submit Article' step ... be sure to check carefully both the title/abstract (metadata) and the processed files. If you see any errors or are unhappy with the formatting then correct them or contact arXiv administrators if there are problems you cannot resolve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the submission preview/processed-files view to verify the output; resolve issues prior to final submit to avoid having to unsubmit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unsubmit to correct errors prior to announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: If [you] discover an error after submission but before public announcement then select the Unsubmit icon next to the submission on your user page to return it to the incomplete status allowing modification and later resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unsubmitting removes the article from the processing queue; resubmission time affects announcement ordering. Use unsubmit to fix mistakes before public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement timing and daily schedule (16:00/20:00 rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each day's submissions before 16:00 US Eastern time Monday through Friday are not made available to the general public until 20:00 US Eastern time Sunday through Thursday. Examples: a Monday before 16:00 becomes publicly available after 20:00 that day and appears in Tuesday AM mailing; Friday before 16:00 appears after 20:00 Sunday etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the 16:00 cutoff and the 20:00 release window; submission time and edits around the cutoff affect when your paper is announced and which day's mailing it appears in.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission order determined by last final 'Submit' time; edits reset order
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions are assigned identifiers and appear in the listings in order based on the submission time (the last time the 'Submit' button was selected). An edit and subsequent 'Submit' will reset this time and thus change position in the listings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you edit and resubmit, you change your place in the day's listing. Edits between 16:00 and 20:00 will remove the submission from that day's announcements and delay it until the next day.

rubrics_metrics.name: Edits before public announcement do not create additional versions
rubrics_metrics.description: Edits before an article is publicly announced will not generate additional versions. The date stamp associated with the submission will be the time that the final 'Submit Article' step is completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make all desired corrections prior to the public announcement to avoid multiple version records; replacing the original submission is preferred to creating a new submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not create a new submission for corrections or errata; replace original
rubrics_metrics.description: DO NOT make a new submission for a corrected article or for an erratum. Rather replace the original submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the replace/edit workflow to submit corrections or errata so the submission history remains coherent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author responsibility and prohibition of third-party submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Because putting articles on arXiv entails certain responsibilities, authors must make their own submissions. Third-party submissions (by secretaries for example) are often the ones that cause the most problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit authors should handle their own uploads to ensure accuracy and responsibility. There are special instructions for third-party submission; consult those if unavoidable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required submission metadata: institutional affiliation and report numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: The following information is also required for submission: Institutional affiliation for the author(s) must be provided. Official report number(s) from the author(s) institution(s) must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide complete institutional affiliation(s) and any official report numbers as part of the submission metadata; omission may impede processing or indexing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official versions are made publicly available
rubrics_metrics.description: Note further that all official versions of submitted articles are made publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that what you submit (official versions) will be publicly accessible; prepare material accordingly and ensure any sensitive information is handled before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special-case instructions (third-party, index submissions, conference proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special instructions for third party submission and index submissions for conference proceedings (referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some submission types (e.g., third-party uploads, index submissions, conference proceedings) have separate rules—consult the referenced special-instructions pages for those workflows.
